top_news.title: Helpfulness Hurts: Domain-Dependent Degradation of Mid-Trained Compassion Values Under Post-Training
top_news.dek: Standard post-training pipelines like SFT and RL can inadvertently degrade specific values instilled during pre-training.
top_news.brief: Researchers analyzed how different post-training domains affect the retention of compassion values in a Llama 3.1 8B model. They found that applying helpfulness-oriented SFT or RL can erode previously learned values, suggesting that the choice of post-training data significantly impacts model alignment and value stability.
top_news.image_alt: Chart showing value degradation across different post-training datasets

top_news.title: [AINews] OpenAI reports median internal Codex output tokens grew 56x in Research, 32x in Customer Support, 27x in Engineering, and 13x in Legal since November 2025.
top_news.dek: OpenAI reports a massive surge in internal Codex token usage across non-coding departments since late 2025.
top_news.brief: Internal data from OpenAI shows that median Codex output tokens have increased by up to 56x in research and 32x in customer support roles. This shift indicates that AI agents are increasingly handling complex, non-coding tasks within the organization.
top_news.image_alt: Bar chart showing growth of Codex token usage by department

top_news.title: OpenAI's GPT 5.6 rollout now requires US government approval on a "customer by customer basis"
top_news.dek: OpenAI will restrict access to its new GPT-5.6 model to select partners, requiring individual U.S. government approval for each customer.
top_news.brief: Following a recent executive order, OpenAI is implementing a customer-by-customer approval process for GPT-5.6. CEO Sam Altman noted the move is not a long-term strategy, but reflects increasing federal oversight regarding AI model safety and deployment.
top_news.image_alt: OpenAI logo and federal government seal

top_news.title: What happened after 2k people tried to hack my AI assistant
top_news.dek: A public stress test of an AI assistant secured with OpenClaw and Hermes successfully resisted over 6,000 adversarial attempts.
top_news.brief: A developer challenged 2,000 users to extract sensitive data from an AI assistant via email. Despite the high volume of attacks, the system maintained its security boundaries and prevented unauthorized data leaks, demonstrating the robustness of the underlying architecture.
top_news.image_alt: Security testing dashboard showing blocked adversarial prompts

top_news.title: deepreinforce-ai/Ornith-1.0-35B-GGUF (3002 downloads, 159 likes)
top_news.dek: DeepReinforce-AI released Ornith-1.0, a new family of open-source coding models trained using self-improving reinforcement learning.
top_news.brief: Ornith-1.0 includes dense and MoE variants ranging from 9B to 397B parameters. Built on Gemma 4 and Qwen 3.5, the models are optimized for agentic coding tasks and demonstrate competitive performance on benchmarks like SWE-Bench and Terminal-Bench 2.1.

primary.title: Baidu Releases Unlimited OCR, a 3B Model That Keeps the KV Cache Flat for Long-Document Parsing
primary.summary: Baidu open-sourced Unlimited OCR, a 3B-parameter MoE model that parses dozens of document pages in a single forward pass. Its Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA) holds the KV cache constant, so memory and latency stay flat as output grows. It scores 93.23 on OmniDocBench v1.5, beating the DeepSeek OCR baseline by 6.22 points, under an MIT license.
